The Lazarus Pill -- follow-up

By: Eugene Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
........the so-called Lazarus Pill continues to surprise and change lives

Summary:
The so-called Lazarus Pill is a sleeping pill called Stilnox, and it astounded scientists when it was discovered that it could wake people up from deep comas. Carte Blanche reported on the story a few years ago, but since then research continued and the pill was fund to benefit a large number of other conditions as well. It has been beneficial for people with paralysis, cerebral palsy, motor neuron disease, MS and other brain injuries. Dr Wally Nel, who discovered the effect of the pill, is still leading the field in trying to find alternative uses for the pill.

Further information:
Background and new discoveries:
Sienie Viljoen would have had no idea 13 years ago that by giving her comatose son a tablet to make him rest better, she’d be initiating a miracle treatment for patients with brain injuries. City Press reported last month on the remarkable reawakening of Louis Viljoen, who stunned his mother when he emerged from a five-year coma after she gave him a Stilnox sleeping tablet. After reading that report, Nomfundo Nqinana insisted that her husband’s sceptical doctors give him a tablet a day. Five days later, he emerged from his seven-year coma, asking for his son.

Now it appears that the pill not only helps those with traumatic brain injuries, but other conditions as well. A few weeks ago, City Press reported on Dr Cival Mills, who suffers from locked-in syndrome after a crippling brainstem stroke he suffered following a car accident. He also read the report on the Lazarus pill and turned to Sienie Viljoen’s general practitioner, Dr Wally Nel, for advice on using Stilnox. He was given half a tablet and after about 40 minutes, spoke for the first time in 11 years. “Dis ‘n voorreg om te kan praat (It’s a privilege to be able to speak),” he said in a clear voice. The pill is now helping Mills a great deal to become more focused and to enable him to work for longer without tiring as easily.

“We have long suspected that the pill could be effective for other brain-related conditions as well,” said Professor Ralf Clauss, a neurologist who ¬lectured at Medunsa before emigrating to the UK. He treated Louis Viljoen after he woke from his coma and, ¬together with Nel, researched Stilnox’s effects on brain ¬injuries. This week, Nel told City Press he has had remarkable success with a patient who suffers from motor-neuron disease. Mossie Mostert was diagnosed with the same fatal disease as rugby star Joost van der Westhuizen. Nel has been treating him with Stilnox for the last three months, and he is now more mobile and has his sense of humour back.“Not only has taking the pill improved his condition, it also seems the degenerative effect of the condition has been halted. It is unheard of,” said Nel.

Clauss and Nel believe that the pill works by waking up dormant brain tissue.Not all cells die off in an area where an injury occurs. Some cells become dormant and Stilnox somehow reactivates them, improving brain function. “The pill works even decades after an injury”, says Clauss, adding that he and Nel have been studying the pill’s effects on patients with cerebral palsy with remarkable results.

Stilnox also appears to work on those with forms of paralysis. Nel treated swimmer Ryk Neethling’s sister Elsje with the pill. She had childhood cancer and one of her legs was paralysed.“She can now walk without crutches,” he says.

Both Nel and Clauss warn, however, that much research still needs to be done on the pill’s effects.

Another well known patient who benefited from the pill is Pippie Kruger. This is what City Press reported in 2012:

Christmas is coming early for Isabella ‘Pippie’ Kruger and her family and one of the festive season’s biggest miracles is a little pill that’s changing her life. Pippie (3) will be back in hospital on Tuesday for her first operation since a successful skin graft in July gave the little burn victim a new lease on life.

Pippie and her parents, Anice and Erwin, will thus celebrate Christmas Eve tomorrow.
If all goes according to plan, the whole family will then spend a quiet Christmas at home together next week.“We know what Pippie will do. She will build Lego. She is absolutely crazy about it and we are buying up people’s old Lego blocks whenever we can,” says Anice. Pippie’s interest in the building blocks is also a sign of her continued improvement. Helping her in that battle is Stilnox, which has been nicknamed the Lazarus Pill. Stilnox is changing Pippie’s life one dose at a time. Amid the dehydration, the cardiac arrests and the infections in the early days of her ordeal, Pippie also suffered a stroke.This left her right side weakened and her speech impaired. eurologists who examined Pippie said that the damage to her brain was significant, and that Pippie would probably not walk and talk again. In September this year (2012), Anice heard about Stilnox and its effects on all kinds of brain injuries. Anice took Pippie to see Nel a few weeks ago. They decided to give Pippie a quarter of a tablet. When they arrived, Pippie was slow and lethargic, says Anice. They then gave her the quarter tablet and, after about 20 minutes, a noticeable change came over Pippie. “I have seen a lot of miracles in these rooms,” says Nel. “But I have never seen anything like this before. She started to blink rapidly. It was not something she had done before.”
“Pippie also started looking around and paying attention to what was going on around her.” Anice says that when this started to happen she was initially too stunned to think. But it was clear Pippie immediately seemed to be more awake and aware of what was going on around her. “The change is remarkable,” says her mother. Pippie’s tongue was also badly burned in the fire and, as a consequence, she had lost some sensation. The Stilnox pill also seemed to counteract this. “She started to drool and it seemed that she became more aware of her tongue,” says Nel. Anice says Pippie’s tasting ability has also improved since that first dose of Stilnox. A day later, Anice mailed Nel a photo of Pippie sitting upright on her own. That was something she could not do before taking the pill. Anice is convinced the pill has made a huge difference and says she sees small improvements in Pippie virtually every day. Since Pippie started taking the Stilnox, Nel and Dr Ridwan Mia – who did the skin grafts and who is still managing Pippie’s continuing treatment – have been in contact and are together mapping the road ahead, which includes the continued use of Stilnox. Anice is confident the series of miracles she has witnessed this year are far from over. This week, Pippie stood for the first time, supported by her delighted mother. NOTE 2014: In the mean time Anice has stopped giving Pippie Stilnox as she believes the less medication she gets the better.

Viewing Notes:
Viewing notes: Wynand
15 January 2pm

Lazarus pill:
We need to know earlier that Elrico is not a normal kid. Establish how bad he was first. “This is Elrico...”. Make it clearer that he is not normal to start with. This is why him saying he can now whistle is strange.
Anti histamine repeat. The mom explains it and then we explain in voice again that the mom gave him the Stilnox by mistake, thinking it is anti-histamine. Feels repetitive.
NB: Say there have been negative side effects reported too and should only be used under the guidance of a doctor and under medical supervision..
Dark shots in passage - Dr Wally with Devi. Lighten up slightly in grading.
Check grammar on Skype comment.

Press Release:


Lazarus Pill
Stilnox – a sleeping tablet - was dubbed the Lazarus Pill when, through a peculiar side-effect, it woke patients from deep comas. Now, Carte Blanche follows up on the increasing applications of this so-called miracle pill as it brings hope to people with paralysis, cerebral palsy and even brain injuries.


Script:


Elruco:
It woke me up completely. I felt energy that I never felt before. I could hear better, I could see better, I could speak more clearly. My lip movement improved. I can actually whistle now. I could never really whistle before and my eye to hand co-ordination is much better. I can actually catch a ball and through a ball and through frisby now.

V/O:
This is 17 year old Elruco du Plessis. He lives with his mother Runel in Vereeniging in Gauteng. Throughout his life he has struggled to keep up with his peers. This started on the day he was born prematurely at 32 weeks. Doctors only gave the tiny baby a 5% chance of survival.

Runel:
He was born with a pseudomona lung infection. He had blood transfusions, I think two. He was ventilated for three weeks where he was never without any infection. And for five weeks he was still in an incubator

V/O:
It was a miracle that Elruco survived at all. But he clung to life. As a child his physical development was much slower than normal, and despite his parents’ love and attention he seemed unable to connect with others. Socially he was very awkward and struggled at school.

Elruco:
It felt like I wasn't going anywhere. It felt like I didn't matter. It felt like I was basically unnecessary in the world. I was basically in my own little box.

V/O:
But, his life changed in an instant when, three months ago, his mother gave him a Stilnox sleeping tablet by mistake when he complained about a headache. At the time Runel was helping Elruco with his homework when a sudden and unexpected change came over him.

Runel:
Within twenty minutes, while we were working, he said to me “Mom, what did you give me to drink. So I said to him I gave you a anti-histamine. He said “No, it must be something else”. I said “But why?” He said “But I feel different and the work is easier” And he finished that task within ten minutes.

Elruco:
I felt as if I could hear and see things more clearly than before.

V/O:
It was an instant and massive change. Elruco’s personality changed. Within minutes he could do things on a physical and mental level that he was unable to do before taking the pill. And the changes also impacted his emotions.

Elruco:
I was comfortable around a lot of people which I never was before. shy as I used to be.

V/O:
On that very weekend he did something without prompting that he had never dared to do before – he reached out to people.

Runel:
He arranged a whole weekend for himself and he went out with friends, he slept over and he had a whole social experience that weekend. And I was like stunned, I thought what is this?

V/O:
For them it was a miracle. Elruco’s life had changed overnight. He even started to hug his mother, something he had never done before.

Elruco and Runel read up on Stilnox and discovered that that it was not the first time that the pill seemed to work magic.

Carte Blanche has reported on Stilnox in the past. Fourteen years ago Sienie Viljoen gave her son Louis, who had been in a coma for 3 years, half a Stilnox tablet and he miraculously emerged from the coma. It was medically unprecedented. She reported this to their GP, Dr Wally Nel, and he brought it to the attention of the medical world. He and Prof Ralph Clauss, based at Medunsa, have been doing research on the effects of Stilnox ever since. Ralf and Wally have come to the conclusion that instead of making patients with brain damage sleep, it had the opposite effect. It actually activated dormant brain cells and increased brain function.

Runel made an appointment with Dr Nel to consult him about their experience with Stilnox.

LINK:
Over the years Dr Wally was also interested to see what effect Stilnox could have on other brain related conditions. So he was not surprised when Ronelle contacted him.

V/O:
We visited Dr Wally at his practice. He had seen Elruco twice and had prescribed more Stillnox. Even he was astounded at the changes in his patient after Elruco had started taking the pill.

Wally:
I really didn't recognised him. He put on 14 kilos. He is open, his face is open. Eyes is the sole of your body. I could look into his eyes, he didn't look away. I didn't recognise him. For sure not.

DEVI:
When we last spoke Dr Wally the theory was that Stilnox wakes up dormant brain cells in damaged parts of the brain. But their continued research now shows that there is actually more to it.

V/O:
It seems that Stilnox not only benefits people with brain damage, but actually has beneficial effects for all kinds of conditions related to the central nervous system.

V/O:
Heidi Twilley runs a music school in Klerksdorp. In 2003 she was diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis. She started to walk with difficulty, she tired easily and could not function as before.

Dr Wally:
Now multiple sclerosis is a horrible thing. Its a degenerative state of your nervous system, whereever. Eventually it leads to paralysis and eventually it leads to death.

Heidi:
I was in constant pain. All day long.

V/O:
Then she heard about Dr Wally and Stilnox. He prescribed the pill and as for so many others, the tablet had an amazing effect.

Wally:
The last time I saw her she walked in there and the first thing she said was : Dr Nel, I can jump.

Heidi:
The difference between can I walk or cant I walk is Stilnox

V/O:
Heidi got her life back and can now again perform physical activities with her music students.

Heidi:
Before Stilnox I wasn’t able to do what I did today. I was not at all. And Im fine! I’ll be able to work another 10 years.

V/O:
Over the years Dr Wally Nel and Prof Ralf Clauss, have continued their research into the working and effects of Stilnox. Ralf now lives in the UK and they have discovered something new about the long term effects of the drug.

We Skyped with Prof Clauss and he told us that a patient called Wayne had shown permanent improvement after being on Stilnox for some years. Stilnox is also called Zolpidem .

Ralf:
Wayne is functioning almost as well off Zolpidem as he is functioning on Zolpidem. So the hope is there that we can stop the medication at some time and he could still function normally.

Devi:
But the common belief is that the brain cannot heal itself.

Ralf:
It seems that the brain is capable of healing itself after the long term Zolpidem that was given to him. So there can be changes in the brain.

V/O:
This is an unprecedented finding and Ralf and Wally are currently doing further studies to confirm this.

However, what is certain, is that Stilnox definitely has major effects on all kinds of conditions that are associated with the nervous system.

Hanna Eloff faced a life as a completely disabled person when she was diagnosed with a rare spinal cord condition.

Hanna:
I got transverse myelitis. This is like infection in the spinal cord. Then I went completely paralysed from my waist down.

V/O:
She lost her mobility and independence, and a severe blow to her was that she could not play the organ any more – something she really loved doing. Wheelchair-bound she went to see Dr Wally.

Wally:
Previously we would have said, with the transverse myelitis, sorry for you. Go for your fisio, go for your occupational therapy and that’s it.

V/O:
But Wally had an ace up his sleeve. He also supplemented her physiotherapy with Stilnox.

Hanna:
They gave me half a tablet. I was sitting there for 2 hours and nothing happened. And that evening I went to bed and in the night when I woke up I heard a funny sound in my head. Like that! And then suddenly it was all lightened up. It seems like you switched on a light in a very dark room.

V/O:
From that moment Hanna’s life was back on track. For her it was a miracle. She could use her hands again, she could walk without assistance and she is even able to ride her bicycle. But most importantly, she could again play her beloved organ with both hands and feet.

Devi:
So would you say that you are living an almost normal life?

Hanna:
Yes, oh yes I do. A little bit slower than always but I can do everything. With a little more effort I can drive my car, I go shopping, I do my homework.

Devi:
You ride your bicycle.

Hanna:
Ja, I ride my bicycle. I do my home work here, I do my cooking, my washing, I can bath myself. I love life.

Devi:
This is just the beginning?

Wally:
Fifteen years, and I think the beginning is now.

V/O:
However, both Dr Wally Nel and Professor Ralf Clauss warn that Stilnox should only be taken under strict medical supervision as it could have serious side effects.

Link:
It seems that the story of the amazing Lazarus Pill as Stilnox has been called, is far from over.

V/O:
A chance discovery by a devoted mother who refused to give up on her only son so many years ago, continues to touch the lives of countless people.

It allows some to dance again……….

To others it has brought a Song of Joy……….

And to Elruco it represents a new life ……….

Elruco:
I don’t know where I'm going, but I know I’m going somewhere. Before I always thought I was on a road to nowhere.

V/O: This is 17 year old Elruco du Plessis. He lives with his mother Runel in Vereeniging in Gauteng. Throughout his life he has struggled to keep up with his peers. This started on the day he was born prematurely at 32 weeks. Doctors only gave the tiny baby a 5% chance of survival. Runel: He was born with a pseudomona lung infection. He had blood transfusions, I think two. He was ventilated for three weeks where he was never without any infection. And for five weeks he was still in an incubator V/O: It was a miracle that Elruco survived at all. But he clung to life. As a child his physical development was much slower than normal, and despite his parents’ love and attention he seemed unable to connect with others. Socially he was very awkward and struggled at school. Elruco: It felt like I wasn't going anywhere. It felt like I didn't matter. It felt like I was basically unnecessary in the world. I was basically in my own little box. V/O: But, his life changed in an instant when, three months ago, his mother gave him a Stilnox sleeping tablet by mistake when he complained about a headache. At the time Runel was helping Elruco with his homework when a sudden and unexpected change came over him. Runel: Within twenty minutes, while we were working, he said to me “Mom, what did you give me to drink. So I said to him I gave you a anti-histamine. He said “No, it must be something else”. I said “But why?” He said “But I feel different and the work is easier” And he finished that task within ten minutes. Elruco: I felt as if I could hear and see things more clearly than before. V/O: It was an instant and massive change. Elruco’s personality changed. Within minutes he could do things on a physical and mental level that he was unable to do before taking the pill. And the changes also impacted his emotions. Elruco: I was comfortable around a lot of people which I never was before. shy as I used to be. V/O: On that very weekend he did something without prompting that he had never dared to do before – he reached out to people. Runel: He arranged a whole weekend for himself and he went out with friends, he slept over and he had a whole social experience that weekend. And I was like stunned, I thought what is this? V/O: For them it was a miracle. Elruco’s life had changed overnight. He even started to hug his mother, something he had never done before. Elruco and Runel read up on Stilnox and discovered that that it was not the first time that the pill seemed to work magic. Carte Blanche has reported on Stilnox in the past. Fourteen years ago Sienie Viljoen gave her son Louis, who had been in a coma for 3 years, half a Stilnox tablet and he miraculously emerged from the coma. It was medically unprecedented. She reported this to their GP, Dr Wally Nel, and he brought it to the attention of the medical world. He and Prof Ralph Clauss, based at Medunsa, have been doing research on the effects of Stilnox ever since. Ralf and Wally have come to the conclusion that instead of making patients with brain damage sleep, it had the opposite effect. It actually activated dormant brain cells and increased brain function. Runel made an appointment with Dr Nel to consult him about their experience with Stilnox. LINK: Over the years Dr Wally was also interested to see what effect Stilnox could have on other brain related conditions. So he was not surprised when Ronelle contacted him. V/O: We visited Dr Wally at his practice. He had seen Elruco twice and had prescribed more Stillnox. Even he was astounded at the changes in his patient after Elruco had started taking the pill. Wally: I really didn't recognised him. He put on 14 kilos. He is open, his face is open. Eyes is the sole of your body. I could look into his eyes, he didn't look away. I didn't recognise him. For sure not. DEVI: When we last spoke Dr Wally the theory was that Stilnox wakes up dormant brain cells in damaged parts of the brain. But their continued research now shows that there is actually more to it. V/O: It seems that Stilnox not only benefits people with brain damage, but actually has beneficial effects for all kinds of conditions related to the central nervous system. V/O: Heidi Twilley runs a music school in Klerksdorp. In 2003 she was diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis. She started to walk with difficulty, she tired easily and could not function as before. Dr Wally: Now multiple sclerosis is a horrible thing. Its a degenerative state of your nervous system, whereever. Eventually it leads to paralysis and eventually it leads to death. Heidi: I was in constant pain. All day long. V/O: Then she heard about Dr Wally and Stilnox. He prescribed the pill and as for so many others, the tablet had an amazing effect. Wally: The last time I saw her she walked in there and the first thing she said was : Dr Nel, I can jump. Heidi: The difference between can I walk or cant I walk is Stilnox V/O: Heidi got her life back and can now again perform physical activities with her music students. Heidi: Before Stilnox I wasn’t able to do what I did today. I was not at all. And Im fine! I’ll be able to work another 10 years. V/O: Over the years Dr Wally Nel and Prof Ralf Clauss, have continued their research into the working and effects of Stilnox. Ralf now lives in the UK and they have discovered something new about the long term effects of the drug. We Skyped with Prof Clauss and he told us that a patient called Wayne had shown permanent improvement after being on Stilnox for some years. Stilnox is also called Zolpidem . Ralf: Wayne is functioning almost as well off Zolpidem as he is functioning on Zolpidem. So the hope is there that we can stop the medication at some time and he could still function normally. Devi: But the common belief is that the brain cannot heal itself. Ralf: It seems that the brain is capable of healing itself after the long term Zolpidem that was given to him. So there can be changes in the brain. V/O: This is an unprecedented finding and Ralf and Wally are currently doing further studies to confirm this. However, what is certain, is that Stilnox definitely has major effects on all kinds of conditions that are associated with the nervous system. Hanna Eloff faced a life as a completely disabled person when she was diagnosed with a rare spinal cord condition. Hanna: I got transverse myelitis. This is like infection in the spinal cord. Then I went completely paralysed from my waist down. V/O: She lost her mobility and independence, and a severe blow to her was that she could not play the organ any more – something she really loved doing. Wheelchair-bound she went to see Dr Wally. Wally: Previously we would have said, with the transverse myelitis, sorry for you. Go for your fisio, go for your occupational therapy and that’s it. V/O: But Wally had an ace up his sleeve. He also supplemented her physiotherapy with Stilnox. Hanna: They gave me half a tablet. I was sitting there for 2 hours and nothing happened. And that evening I went to bed and in the night when I woke up I heard a funny sound in my head. Like that! And then suddenly it was all lightened up. It seems like you switched on a light in a very dark room. V/O: From that moment Hanna’s life was back on track. For her it was a miracle. She could use her hands again, she could walk without assistance and she is even able to ride her bicycle. But most importantly, she could again play her beloved organ with both hands and feet. Devi: So would you say that you are living an almost normal life? Hanna: Yes, oh yes I do. A little bit slower than always but I can do everything. With a little more effort I can drive my car, I go shopping, I do my homework. Devi: You ride your bicycle. Hanna: Ja, I ride my bicycle. I do my home work here, I do my cooking, my washing, I can bath myself. I love life. Devi: This is just the beginning? Wally: Fifteen years, and I think the beginning is now. V/O: However, both Dr Wally Nel and Professor Ralf Clauss warn that Stilnox should only be taken under strict medical supervision as it could have serious side effects. Link: It seems that the story of the amazing Lazarus Pill as Stilnox has been called, is far from over. V/O: A chance discovery by a devoted mother who refused to give up on her only son so many years ago, continues to touch the lives of countless people. It allows some to dance again………. To others it has brought a Song of Joy………. And to Elruco it represents a new life ………. Elruco: I don’t know where I'm going, but I know I’m going somewhere. Before I always thought I was on a road to nowhere. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): ........the so-called Lazarus Pill continues to surprise and change lives
metadata.Summary: The so-called Lazarus Pill is a sleeping pill called Stilnox, and it astounded scientists when it was discovered that it could wake people up from deep comas. Carte Blanche reported on the story a few years ago, but since then research continued and the pill was fund to benefit a large number of other conditions as well. It has been beneficial for people with paralysis, cerebral palsy, motor neuron disease, MS and other brain injuries. Dr Wally Nel, who discovered the effect of the pill, is still leading the field in trying to find alternative uses for the pill.
metadata.Further information: Background and new discoveries: Sienie Viljoen would have had no idea 13 years ago that by giving her comatose son a tablet to make him rest better, she’d be initiating a miracle treatment for patients with brain injuries. City Press reported last month on the remarkable reawakening of Louis Viljoen, who stunned his mother when he emerged from a five-year coma after she gave him a Stilnox sleeping tablet. After reading that report, Nomfundo Nqinana insisted that her husband’s sceptical doctors give him a tablet a day. Five days later, he emerged from his seven-year coma, asking for his son. Now it appears that the pill not only helps those with traumatic brain injuries, but other conditions as well. A few weeks ago, City Press reported on Dr Cival Mills, who suffers from locked-in syndrome after a crippling brainstem stroke he suffered following a car accident. He also read the report on the Lazarus pill and turned to Sienie Viljoen’s general practitioner, Dr Wally Nel, for advice on using Stilnox. He was given half a tablet and after about 40 minutes, spoke for the first time in 11 years. “Dis ‘n voorreg om te kan praat (It’s a privilege to be able to speak),” he said in a clear voice. The pill is now helping Mills a great deal to become more focused and to enable him to work for longer without tiring as easily. “We have long suspected that the pill could be effective for other brain-related conditions as well,” said Professor Ralf Clauss, a neurologist who ¬lectured at Medunsa before emigrating to the UK. He treated Louis Viljoen after he woke from his coma and, ¬together with Nel, researched Stilnox’s effects on brain ¬injuries. This week, Nel told City Press he has had remarkable success with a patient who suffers from motor-neuron disease. Mossie Mostert was diagnosed with the same fatal disease as rugby star Joost van der Westhuizen. Nel has been treating him with Stilnox for the last three months, and he is now more mobile and has his sense of humour back.“Not only has taking the pill improved his condition, it also seems the degenerative effect of the condition has been halted. It is unheard of,” said Nel. Clauss and Nel believe that the pill works by waking up dormant brain tissue.Not all cells die off in an area where an injury occurs. Some cells become dormant and Stilnox somehow reactivates them, improving brain function. “The pill works even decades after an injury”, says Clauss, adding that he and Nel have been studying the pill’s effects on patients with cerebral palsy with remarkable results. Stilnox also appears to work on those with forms of paralysis. Nel treated swimmer Ryk Neethling’s sister Elsje with the pill. She had childhood cancer and one of her legs was paralysed.“She can now walk without crutches,” he says. Both Nel and Clauss warn, however, that much research still needs to be done on the pill’s effects. Another well known patient who benefited from the pill is Pippie Kruger. This is what City Press reported in 2012: Christmas is coming early for Isabella ‘Pippie’ Kruger and her family and one of the festive season’s biggest miracles is a little pill that’s changing her life. Pippie (3) will be back in hospital on Tuesday for her first operation since a successful skin graft in July gave the little burn victim a new lease on life. Pippie and her parents, Anice and Erwin, will thus celebrate Christmas Eve tomorrow. If all goes according to plan, the whole family will then spend a quiet Christmas at home together next week.“We know what Pippie will do. She will build Lego. She is absolutely crazy about it and we are buying up people’s old Lego blocks whenever we can,” says Anice. Pippie’s interest in the building blocks is also a sign of her continued improvement. Helping her in that battle is Stilnox, which has been nicknamed the Lazarus Pill. Stilnox is changing Pippie’s life one dose at a time. Amid the dehydration, the cardiac arrests and the infections in the early days of her ordeal, Pippie also suffered a stroke.This left her right side weakened and her speech impaired. eurologists who examined Pippie said that the damage to her brain was significant, and that Pippie would probably not walk and talk again. In September this year (2012), Anice heard about Stilnox and its effects on all kinds of brain injuries. Anice took Pippie to see Nel a few weeks ago. They decided to give Pippie a quarter of a tablet. When they arrived, Pippie was slow and lethargic, says Anice. They then gave her the quarter tablet and, after about 20 minutes, a noticeable change came over Pippie. “I have seen a lot of miracles in these rooms,” says Nel. “But I have never seen anything like this before. She started to blink rapidly. It was not something she had done before.” “Pippie also started looking around and paying attention to what was going on around her.” Anice says that when this started to happen she was initially too stunned to think. But it was clear Pippie immediately seemed to be more awake and aware of what was going on around her. “The change is remarkable,” says her mother. Pippie’s tongue was also badly burned in the fire and, as a consequence, she had lost some sensation. The Stilnox pill also seemed to counteract this. “She started to drool and it seemed that she became more aware of her tongue,” says Nel. Anice says Pippie’s tasting ability has also improved since that first dose of Stilnox. A day later, Anice mailed Nel a photo of Pippie sitting upright on her own. That was something she could not do before taking the pill. Anice is convinced the pill has made a huge difference and says she sees small improvements in Pippie virtually every day. Since Pippie started taking the Stilnox, Nel and Dr Ridwan Mia – who did the skin grafts and who is still managing Pippie’s continuing treatment – have been in contact and are together mapping the road ahead, which includes the continued use of Stilnox. Anice is confident the series of miracles she has witnessed this year are far from over. This week, Pippie stood for the first time, supported by her delighted mother. NOTE 2014: In the mean time Anice has stopped giving Pippie Stilnox as she believes the less medication she gets the better.
